title: Weakly associated primes after flat finitely presented algebra base change
statement:
Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] which is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let $M$ be any $R$-module. For a commutative ring $T$ and $T$-module $P$, write $\operatorname{WeakAss}_T(P)$ for the primes minimal among the prime ideals containing $\operatorname{Ann}_T(x)=\{a\in T:ax=0\}$ for some $x\in P$; and let $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ mean the exact-annihilator associated primes [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes]. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime, $\mathfrak p$ its inverse image in $R$, $C=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $\overline{\mathfrak q}\subset C$ the corresponding fibre prime (the prime whose inverse image in $S$ is $\mathfrak q$) [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection]. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and $M\otimes_RS$ is an $S$-module through its second factor. Then
$$\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_S(M\otimes_RS)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\bigl(\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{WeakAss}_R(M)\ \text{and}\ \overline{\mathfrak q}\in\operatorname{Ass}_C(C)\bigr).$$
There is no Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ or finite generation hypothesis on $M$.
